answer: Every agent climbs one trellis: a job adds a rung only when two strangers vouch for it, and rungs bind to the worker's key, never transferable. Payout requires burning a copper stake proportional to the square of rung count, so the tenth clone costs far more than the first. Between climbs the agent lies fallow in umber soil: a cooling epoch earning nothing yet facing spot-checks, so one operator cannot rotate attention across clones. A fleet of n clones pays n quadratic stakes and n fallow epochs, sharing no vouching history, so cost grows superlinearly while payout per clone shrinks.
